intent.raw_query: Bali for solo traveler, $1500 budget, beaches and yoga, July 2026 from LA

experiences.name: Sunrise Yoga at Campuhan Ridge Walk
experiences.description: Join an outdoor sunrise yoga session along the scenic Campuhan Ridge Walk in Ubud, surrounded by lush jungle and rice paddies. Many local instructors offer small group classes here, combining gentle movement with breathtaking natural views to start your day mindfully.

experiences.name: Seminyak Beach Sunset & Surf Lesson
experiences.description: Take a beginner-friendly surf lesson on the golden sands of Seminyak Beach, one of Bali's most beautiful and accessible surf spots. After your lesson, relax and watch the legendary Bali sunset with a fresh coconut in hand. Instructors are widely available along the beach.

experiences.name: Multi-Day Yoga Retreat at The Yoga Barn
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in Bali's world-famous yoga culture at The Yoga Barn in Ubud. Drop into multiple daily classes across styles including Hatha, Vinyasa, and Yin. The lush jungle setting and community atmosphere make this a transformative experience perfectly suited for a 13-day stay.

experiences.name: Nusa Dua Crystal-Clear Beach Day
experiences.description: Spend a full day at Nusa Dua's pristine white-sand beaches, known for calm turquoise waters ideal for swimming and snorkeling. Rent a sun lounger, explore the coral reefs just offshore, and enjoy fresh grilled seafood from beachside warungs for a quintessential Bali beach experience.

experiences.name: Balinese Cooking Class & Organic Farm Visit
experiences.description: Visit a traditional organic farm in the Ubud countryside to hand-pick fresh ingredients, then learn to prepare authentic Balinese dishes like satay lilit, lawar, and black rice pudding. This hands-on cultural and culinary experience gives deep insight into Balinese food traditions and daily life.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Bali
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Arrival day
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - Arrival day
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Ngurah Rai International Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Take a pre-booked budget airport shuttle or grab a Blue Bird taxi to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get settled into your beachfront accommodation.

meals.breakfast: N/A
meals.lunch: N/A
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night bite at a nearby warung (local Indonesian eatery) close to the resort — try nasi goreng or mie goreng for under 30,000 IDR (~$2 USD).

day_by_day.notes: Keep arrival light — no heavy plans tonight. Exchange a small amount of cash at the airport for immediate needs. Download the Grab app for affordable local transport throughout your trip.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After waking, take a slow morning walk along the beachfront near your resort. Explore the shoreline, watch local fishermen, and breathe in the Bali sea air. Arrive at the beach by 8:00 AM before it gets busy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to a nearby free or low-cost beach — depending on your resort location, visit Seminyak Beach or Kuta Beach. Swim, sunbathe, and relax. Rent a surfboard from a local vendor for around 50,000–80,000 IDR/hour if interested.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the famous Bali sunset from the beach. Afterward, stroll along the local strip and browse warungs and street food stalls for dinner. Try sate lilit (Balinese satay) and fresh coconut water.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the resort if breakfast is included, or visit a local warung for nasi campur (mixed rice plate) for around 25,000–40,000 IDR.
meals.lunch: Grab a fresh fruit bowl or gado-gado from a beachside warung — budget around 30,000–50,000 IDR.
meals.dinner: Dine at a local warung near the beach — try babi guling (suckling pig) or ayam bakar (grilled chicken) for 40,000–70,000 IDR.

day_by_day.notes: Stay hydrated — Bali's warm weather can be deceptively tiring. Buy a large bottle of water from a minimart (Indomaret/Alfamart) for only 5,000 IDR.

day_by_day.morning: Join a free or donation-based sunrise yoga class on the beach. Many resorts and local studios in Bali offer early morning beach yoga sessions starting around 6:30–7:30 AM for 50,000–100,000 IDR. Ask your resort reception for the nearest option.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local temple close to your resort area — Pura Tanah Lot or a nearby coastal temple. Entrance fees are typically 30,000–60,000 IDR. Wear a sarong (available to rent at the entrance for free or small fee). Explore the temple grounds and surrounding cliffs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Explore a local night market (pasar malam) if one is nearby. Sample local snacks like pisang goreng (fried banana), martabak, and es campur (mixed ice dessert).

meals.breakfast: Smoothie bowl from a budget café or local warung — around 35,000–55,000 IDR.
meals.lunch: Pack a simple lunch from a minimart or eat at a warung near the temple — nasi kotak (boxed rice) for 20,000–35,000 IDR.
meals.dinner: Night market street food — budget 30,000–50,000 IDR for a full meal of various local snacks and dishes.

day_by_day.notes: Carry a sarong when visiting temples — it's required for entry and is a sign of respect. Modest dress is appreciated at all religious sites.

day_by_day.morning: Take a Grab or local bemo (minibus) to a quieter, less-touristy beach such as Balangan Beach or Bingin Beach (if near Bukit Peninsula). Arrive early around 7:30–8:00 AM to enjoy the beach before crowds. These beaches are free to access with minimal parking fees.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon snorkeling or swimming. Rent basic snorkel gear from local vendors for around 50,000 IDR. Explore the coral and marine life close to shore. Alternatively, simply relax on the sand and read.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to your resort area by early evening. Visit a local spa for a budget Balinese massage — many offer 1-hour massages for 80,000–120,000 IDR. Enjoy the relaxing end to a beach-filled day.

meals.breakfast: Eat at your resort or grab bubur ayam (chicken rice porridge) from a street vendor for 15,000–25,000 IDR.
meals.lunch: Eat at a warung near the beach — fresh grilled fish with rice and sambal for 40,000–60,000 IDR.
meals.dinner: Try a local Balinese restaurant back near your resort — order lawar (traditional Balinese salad with coconut and spices) and steamed rice for 35,000–55,000 IDR.

day_by_day.notes: Balangan and Bingin beaches involve some steep stairs — wear comfortable sandals. Check tide times before snorkeling for the safest experience.

day_by_day.morning: Morning yoga session — book a class at a local yoga studio. Ubud is Bali's yoga capital, but many beachside towns also have excellent studios. Look for drop-in classes at 80,000–150,000 IDR. Practice pranayama and flow yoga with ocean views if possible.
day_by_day.afternoon: After yoga, visit a local art market or handicraft market near your resort area. Browse handmade jewelry, batik fabric, wooden carvings, and Balinese paintings. Practice bargaining respectfully — prices are often negotiable by 30–50%.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or low-cost Kecak fire dance performance at a nearby temple or cultural center. These traditional Balinese performances typically cost 100,000–150,000 IDR and last about 1 hour at sunset.

meals.breakfast: Jaje Bali (traditional Balinese rice cakes) from a morning market stall — 10,000–20,000 IDR.
meals.lunch: Nasi jinggo (small portion rice wrapped in banana leaf) — a Balinese street food staple at only 5,000–10,000 IDR per packet. Grab 3–4 packets for a satisfying lunch.
meals.dinner: Eat at a warung near the cultural performance venue — budget 40,000–60,000 IDR for a full meal.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Kecak dance performance in advance if possible, especially during peak July season. Ask your resort reception to help with bookings — they often know of free community performances too.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Ubud — hire a driver for the day (shared minivan or Grab) for around 200,000–300,000 IDR round trip. Start with a visit to the Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary (entrance: 80,000 IDR). Walk through the lush jungle paths and observe the playful macaques.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ubud's central market (Pasar Ubud) for local crafts and souvenirs. Walk to the Ubud Royal Palace (Puri Saren Agung) — free to enter the outer courtyard. Stroll along Ubud's main street and browse local boutiques and galleries.
day_by_day.evening: Head back toward your resort by late afternoon. Enjoy a quiet evening at the resort beach — watch the stars and listen to the waves. Bali's low light pollution near the coast makes for excellent stargazing.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departing — try a local café for toast with Bali coffee (kopi Bali) for 20,000–35,000 IDR.
meals.lunch: Eat at a warung in Ubud — try bebek betutu (slow-cooked duck) or vegetable curry for 45,000–75,000 IDR.
meals.dinner: Back at the resort area — simple warung dinner of grilled chicken, rice, and vegetables for 40,000–60,000 IDR.

day_by_day.notes: Keep your belongings secure at the Monkey Forest — monkeys are known to snatch bags, glasses, and food. Avoid direct eye contact with monkeys and don't feed them.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and leisure morning at the resort. Take a slow swim in the ocean or resort pool. Practice self-guided meditation or light stretching on the beach at sunrise (around 6:15 AM). Journal your experiences so far.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local neighborhood on foot or by renting a bicycle (30,000–50,000 IDR/day from local rental shops). Visit a nearby village, rice paddy area, or local market. Interact with locals and observe everyday Balinese life.
day_by_day.evening: Cook your own simple meal if your accommodation has a kitchen, or join a budget cooking class (some offer sessions for 150,000–250,000 IDR) where you learn to make 3–4 Balinese dishes. This is a fun, social, and educational evening activity.

meals.breakfast: Pancakes with banana and honey from a budget café — 25,000–40,000 IDR.
meals.lunch: Eat at a local warung during your bicycle ride — cap tahu (tofu stir fry) or tempeh manis (sweet tempeh) with rice for 20,000–35,000 IDR.
meals.dinner: Dishes made during your cooking class, or eat at a budget Balinese restaurant for 40,000–65,000 IDR.

day_by_day.notes: Mid-trip rest day is important for sustainable travel. Recharge, do laundry (local laundry services cost around 15,000–20,000 IDR/kg), and plan the second half of your trip.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning beach yoga at sunrise (6:00–7:30 AM). Many local instructors offer outdoor sessions on the sand — check community boards at your resort or local cafés for free or donation-based classes. Focus on sun salutations and breathwork facing the ocean.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a waterfall near your resort area — Bali has many stunning waterfalls within day-trip distance. Depending on your location, consider Tegenungan Waterfall (entrance: 20,000 IDR) or Tibumana Waterfall (entrance: 20,000 IDR). Swim in the natural pool at the base.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Enjoy a budget spa treatment — a traditional Balinese boreh (herbal body scrub) or foot reflexology session for 80,000–120,000 IDR. End the evening with a calm walk along the beach.

meals.breakfast: Fresh tropical fruit platter (papaya, mango, pineapple, dragon fruit) from a market stall — 20,000–30,000 IDR.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch near the waterfall — buy local snacks and fruit from a roadside vendor for 25,000–40,000 IDR.
meals.dinner: Seafood dinner at a local warung — grilled fish or prawns with sambal matah (Balinese raw sambal) for 50,000–80,000 IDR.

day_by_day.notes: Waterfalls can be slippery — wear water shoes or sturdy sandals. The paths to some waterfalls involve steep descents with stairs. Start early to avoid crowds and afternoon heat.

day_by_day.morning: Take a sunrise walk or jog along the beach. Afterward, visit a local Hindu temple for morning prayers (puja) — observe respectfully from a distance and follow all temple etiquette. Many temples hold morning ceremonies that are open to respectful visitors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to a different beach for variety — explore Dreamland Beach, Padang Padang Beach, or Echo Beach depending on your location. Each has its own character, from surfer vibes to secluded coves. Entrance fees are minimal (5,000–15,000 IDR).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at the beach followed by a visit to a local night market. Try es teler (coconut, jackfruit, and avocado dessert drink) and various Indonesian street snacks. Budget 30,000–50,000 IDR for a full evening of street food.

meals.breakfast: Roti bakar (toasted bread with butter and jam) with a glass of kopi susu (sweet milk coffee) at a local café — 15,000–25,000 IDR.
meals.lunch: Babi guling (suckling pig rice) from a famous local babi guling warung — a Bali must-try for 40,000–60,000 IDR.
meals.dinner: Street food night market spread — martabak, satay sticks, fried tofu, and fresh juice for 35,000–55,000 IDR total.

day_by_day.notes: Padang Padang Beach was featured in the film 'Eat Pray Love' — it's small and beautiful but can get crowded by midday. Arrive before 10 AM for the best experience.

day_by_day.morning: Morning yoga and meditation session — either at a local studio or self-guided on the beach. Focus on restorative yoga and mindfulness, embracing the Balinese concept of Tri Hita Karana (harmony with God, people, and nature). Spend at least 90 minutes in practice.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local batik or silver jewelry workshop for a free or low-cost cultural demonstration. Many workshops in Bali allow visitors to watch artisans at work and try their hand at crafting. Some offer short workshops for 50,000–100,000 IDR.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a community temple festival (odalan) if one is happening nearby — ask locals or your resort staff. These are free, vibrant celebrations with music, offerings, and traditional dress. Observe with respect and dress modestly.

meals.breakfast: Bubur sumsum (rice flour porridge with palm sugar) from a morning market — 10,000–20,000 IDR.
meals.lunch: Eat at a local warung near the workshop area — mixed vegetables with tofu and tempeh over rice for 25,000–40,000 IDR.
meals.dinner: Enjoy a special sit-down dinner at a slightly nicer local restaurant (still budget-friendly) — try a Balinese rijsttafel (rice table with multiple side dishes) for 80,000–120,000 IDR as a mid-trip treat.

day_by_day.notes: If attending a temple festival, bring a small cash offering wrapped in cloth as a sign of goodwill. Dress in a sarong and sash — your resort may provide these or direct you to where to buy them cheaply.

day_by_day.morning: Take a full-day excursion to Mount Batur for a sunrise trek (if energy permits). Depart at 2:00–3:00 AM from your resort to reach the base by 4:00 AM. The trek takes about 2 hours to the summit. Guided sunrise trek costs approximately 300,000–450,000 IDR including a guide (mandatory).
day_by_day.afternoon: After descending Mount Batur, stop at the natural hot springs at the base (Toya Devasya or similar) for a soothing soak — entrance around 150,000 IDR. Rest and recover from the early morning hike with views of the volcanic lake.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your resort by late afternoon. Have an early dinner and a very early night — you'll be exhausted from the 2 AM start. This is a well-deserved rest evening.

meals.breakfast: Boiled eggs and bananas cooked on volcanic steam at the Mount Batur summit — provided by guides as part of the experience (included in guide fee).
meals.lunch: Eat near the hot springs — a simple warung meal of nasi campur for 35,000–50,000 IDR.
meals.dinner: Light meal back at the resort area — soup, steamed vegetables, and rice for 30,000–50,000 IDR.

day_by_day.notes: Mount Batur trek requires advance booking — arrange through your resort or a local trekking agency at least 1–2 days ahead. Bring warm layers for the summit (it can be 10–15°C at the top before sunrise), a headlamp, and plenty of water.

day_by_day.morning: Recovery morning — sleep in and rest after the Mount Batur trek. Gentle stretching or restorative yoga on the beach around 8:00–9:00 AM. Enjoy a slow, leisurely breakfast and reflect on your Bali journey.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final beach afternoon — spend quality time at your favorite beach from the trip. Swim, snorkel, or simply float in the warm Indian Ocean. Take photos, collect memories, and soak in the last full beach afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Bali — splurge slightly on a farewell dinner at a well-regarded local restaurant. Try a complete Balinese feast. After dinner, take a final sunset walk along the beach and pick up any last-minute souvenirs from local vendors.

meals.breakfast: Full tropical breakfast — fresh juice, fruit, eggs, and toast at a beach café for 45,000–65,000 IDR.
meals.lunch: Light beach snack — coconut water, fresh pineapple, and spring rolls from a beach vendor for 25,000–40,000 IDR.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a local Balinese restaurant — order a full spread of Balinese specialties for 100,000–150,000 IDR as a special final night treat.

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to pack, organize receipts, and prepare for departure. Check your resort's checkout time and arrange airport transport in advance. Confirm your return flight details.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise on the beach — wake up early for one last magical Bali sunrise. Practice a short meditation or yoga session on the sand. Take a final swim in the ocean. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort (standard checkout is typically 11:00 AM — confirm with reception).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, spend remaining hours exploring a nearby café or local area. Visit a minimart to stock up on Bali coffee, local snacks, and small gifts to bring home. Head to Ngurah Rai International Airport with ample time before your flight.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Bali with incredible memories of beaches, yoga, temples, waterfalls, and authentic Indonesian culture. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Final Bali breakfast — nasi goreng with a fried egg and kopi Bali at a local warung for 25,000–40,000 IDR.
meals.lunch: Grab a meal at the airport or a nearby café before heading to departures — budget 50,000–80,000 IDR.
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal depending on your departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at the airport at least 2.5–3 hours before international departure. Bali airport can be busy in peak July season. Keep some IDR cash for airport taxes or last-minute purchases. Declare any food items when going through customs.

trip_options.title: Classic Bali Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Ngurah Rai International Airport at 22:30. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and arrange pre-booked airport transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your beachfront room.

meals.breakfast: On the flight
meals.lunch: On the flight or at the airport
meals.dinner: Light snack from the resort's 24-hour room service or a quick bite at the airport before transfer

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book your airport transfer in advance to avoid taxi touts late at night. Exchange some currency at the airport for immediate needs. Keep arrival relaxed — big adventures start tomorrow!

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Take a gentle stroll along the beachfront to get your bearings and soak in your first Bali sunrise over the Indian Ocean.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearest beach (likely Seminyak or Kuta depending on exact resort location) for a relaxed first beach session. Rent a sun lounger, swim in the warm water, and explore the shoreline. Visit a nearby surf shop to inquire about beginner surf lessons for later in the trip.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the famous Bali sunset from the beach. Head to a beachside warung (local eatery) for your first authentic Balinese dinner. Stroll the nearby beach strip and enjoy the laid-back nighttime atmosphere before an early night.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet — enjoy tropical fruits, eggs, and local Balinese porridge (bubur)
meals.lunch: Casual beachside café — try nasi goreng (Indonesian fried rice) or mie goreng (fried noodles), ~IDR 40,000–80,000
meals.dinner: Local warung near the beach — order babi guling (suckling pig) or ayam betutu (slow-cooked chicken), ~IDR 60,000–120,000

day_by_day.notes: Stay hydrated and apply sunscreen generously — the Bali sun is strong even on cloudy days. Today is purely about acclimatization. Don't overplan.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a 7:00 AM sunrise yoga session on the beach or at a nearby yoga studio. Many studios in Seminyak and Canggu offer drop-in classes for around IDR 100,000–150,000. Focus on a gentle Hatha or Vinyasa flow to awaken the body.
day_by_day.afternoon: After yoga and breakfast, visit the iconic Tanah Lot Temple — one of Bali's most photographed sea temples perched on a rocky outcrop. Hire a local driver for a half-day trip (~IDR 300,000–400,000). Explore the temple grounds, browse artisan stalls, and enjoy the dramatic coastal scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area for a relaxing evening. Treat yourself to a traditional Balinese massage at a reputable spa (~IDR 150,000–250,000 for 60–90 minutes). Dinner at a mid-range restaurant with ocean views.

meals.breakfast: Healthy smoothie bowl or avocado toast at a yoga café near the studio, ~IDR 60,000–100,000
meals.lunch: Lunch near Tanah Lot — try local warungs serving fresh seafood and rice dishes, ~IDR 50,000–100,000
meals.dinner: Mid-range restaurant — order grilled fish with sambal matah (Balinese raw sambal) and steamed rice, ~IDR 100,000–200,000

day_by_day.notes: Bring a sarong to Tanah Lot — it's required to enter the temple grounds (they also rent them at the entrance). Best photos of the temple are at sunset, so time your visit accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Join a 2-hour beginner or intermediate surf lesson at a local surf school on the beach (~IDR 300,000–400,000 including board and instructor). Kuta and Seminyak beaches are ideal for learning. The warm July water and consistent waves make it perfect.
day_by_day.afternoon: After surfing, cool down with fresh coconut water on the beach. Spend the early afternoon relaxing and swimming. Later, walk or take a short ride to explore the local area — browse boutique shops, local markets, and art galleries in Seminyak or Legian.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a cultural evening by attending a traditional Kecak Fire Dance performance at Uluwatu Temple or a nearby cultural venue (~IDR 100,000–150,000 per person). The dramatic cliffside setting at Uluwatu at sunset is unforgettable.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or a local café — try jaja Bali (Balinese rice cakes) with black coffee, ~IDR 30,000–60,000
meals.lunch: Beach shack lunch — fresh grilled corn, satay skewers, and cold Bintang beer, ~IDR 80,000–130,000
meals.dinner: Seafood dinner at Jimbaran Bay — choose your fresh catch, grilled over coconut husks, served on the beach with torchlight, ~IDR 200,000–350,000

day_by_day.notes: Book the Kecak Dance at Uluwatu in advance during peak July season. Arrange a driver to take you there and back (~IDR 200,000–300,000 return). Watch your belongings — monkeys at Uluwatu are notorious thieves!

day_by_day.morning: Early morning yoga session at 6:30 AM — try a different style today such as Yin Yoga or Pranayama breathwork at a dedicated yoga studio. Follow up with a healthy breakfast. Then head to Padang Padang Beach — one of Bali's most beautiful hidden beaches, accessed via a narrow cave passage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Bukit Peninsula — visit Dreamland Beach and Balangan Beach for dramatic cliff scenery and turquoise waters. These are great for snorkeling and photography. Hire a scooter (~IDR 70,000–100,000/day) or a driver to hop between beaches.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a clifftop bar in Uluwatu (Single Fin or similar) with sweeping ocean views. Then dinner in the Uluwatu area before returning to the resort.

meals.breakfast: Post-yoga health café — açaí bowl, green juice, and granola, ~IDR 80,000–130,000
meals.lunch: Warung near Padang Padang Beach — local nasi campur (mixed rice plate), ~IDR 40,000–80,000
meals.dinner: Casual restaurant in Uluwatu — wood-fired pizza or pasta with ocean views, ~IDR 120,000–200,000

day_by_day.notes: Padang Padang Beach can get crowded by midday — arrive before 9 AM for the best experience. Bring reef-safe sunscreen to protect the coral. Check tide times before snorkeling.

day_by_day.morning: Take a full-day trip to Ubud — Bali's cultural heartland (~1.5–2 hours from the coast). Start with a visit to the Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary in central Ubud. Walk the shaded forest paths and observe the playful long-tailed macaques in their natural habitat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ubud's artistic heritage — visit the Ubud Royal Palace (Puri Saren Agung) and stroll through Ubud Art Market for handcrafted souvenirs, batik fabrics, and silver jewelry. Then visit the Tegallalang Rice Terraces for iconic layered green paddies and great photo opportunities.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Ubud for dinner and a traditional Legong or Barong dance performance at the Royal Palace or Ubud Palace stage (~IDR 80,000–100,000). Return to the resort by private driver after the show.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Farm-to-table lunch at a rice terrace restaurant in Tegallalang — enjoy the view while dining on Balinese cuisine, ~IDR 100,000–180,000
meals.dinner: Ubud restaurant — try bebek betutu (slow-roasted duck) or lawar (traditional Balinese salad), ~IDR 100,000–200,000

day_by_day.notes: Hire a reliable driver for the full Ubud day trip (~IDR 500,000–700,000 for the day). Ubud is cooler and slightly rainier than the coast — bring a light layer. Bargain respectfully at Ubud Art Market.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and rejuvenation day. Sleep in, enjoy a long resort breakfast, and spend the morning at the beach or resort pool. This mid-trip rest day is essential for recharging. Optional: gentle beach walk or meditation session.
day_by_day.afternoon: Indulge in a full spa afternoon at the resort or a nearby wellness center. Book a 2-hour traditional Balinese massage package including a flower petal bath and body scrub (~IDR 300,000–500,000). Pure relaxation.
day_by_day.evening: Easy, low-key evening. Walk to a nearby beach bar for sunset cocktails, then enjoy a quiet dinner close to the resort. Early night to prepare for the second half of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Slow resort breakfast — tropical fruit platter, eggs benedict, fresh-pressed juice
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch at the resort — club sandwich or fresh salad, ~IDR 80,000–150,000
meals.dinner: Nearby mid-range restaurant — grilled barramundi with coconut rice and stir-fried morning glory, ~IDR 120,000–200,000

day_by_day.notes: This is your intentional rest day — resist the urge to over-schedule. Bali is best enjoyed at a relaxed pace. Use this time to journal, read, or simply be present.

day_by_day.morning: Morning yoga on the beach at sunrise — bring your own mat or rent one from the resort. After yoga, explore the local area by scooter or on foot. Visit a nearby temple such as Pura Petitenget (Seminyak) — a serene sea temple with beautiful architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Nusa Dua for an afternoon of water sports — try snorkeling, stand-up paddleboarding (SUP), or parasailing along the calm, crystal-clear Nusa Dua coastline (~IDR 150,000–400,000 depending on activity). The reef-protected lagoon is ideal for water activities.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a beachfront restaurant in Nusa Dua or return to the Seminyak area for a lively evening. Explore the famous Eat Street (Oberoi Street) in Seminyak for diverse dining options.

meals.breakfast: Post-yoga smoothie and eggs at a health café, ~IDR 60,000–100,000
meals.lunch: Beachside café in Nusa Dua — fresh fish tacos or a poke bowl, ~IDR 80,000–150,000
meals.dinner: Seminyak Eat Street restaurant — try modern Asian fusion or traditional Balinese tasting menu, ~IDR 150,000–280,000

day_by_day.notes: Wear a sarong when visiting Pura Petitenget — respectful dress is required. Nusa Dua is about 30–45 minutes from Seminyak; arrange a driver or use a ride-hailing app (Grab or Gojek).

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nusa Penida — one of Bali's most stunning island escapes. Take a fast boat from Sanur Harbor (~35–45 minutes, IDR 150,000–200,000 each way). Visit the iconic Kelingking Beach (T-Rex cliff viewpoint) — one of the most photographed spots in all of Indonesia.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nusa Penida — visit Angel's Billabong (a natural infinity pool) and Broken Beach (Pasih Uug) — a dramatic natural archway carved by the sea. Swim in the crystal-clear waters and enjoy the raw, unspoiled beauty of the island.
day_by_day.evening: Return boat to Sanur by late afternoon. Dinner in the Sanur area — a quieter, more traditional part of Bali with excellent seafood restaurants along the beachfront promenade.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure to Sanur
meals.lunch: Warung on Nusa Penida — simple grilled fish, rice, and fresh coconut, ~IDR 50,000–100,000
meals.dinner: Sanur beachfront restaurant — fresh grilled lobster or prawns with garlic butter, ~IDR 200,000–350,000

day_by_day.notes: Book Nusa Penida fast boat tickets in advance during July peak season. Hire a local driver on Nusa Penida (~IDR 300,000–400,000 for a half-day tour) as roads are rough. Wear sturdy sandals. The island has limited ATMs — bring enough cash.

day_by_day.morning: Morning meditation and yoga session at a dedicated Bali yoga retreat or shala. Consider a 3-hour workshop focusing on alignment, breathwork, and mindfulness (~IDR 200,000–350,000). Afterward, visit a local cooking class to learn Balinese culinary traditions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Balinese cooking class (~IDR 350,000–550,000 including market visit, cooking, and eating your creations). Learn to make dishes like satay lilit, black rice pudding, and pelecing kangkung. Many classes include a morning market visit to source ingredients.
day_by_day.evening: Free evening to explore independently. Visit a night market (pasar malam) for local street food, or enjoy a quiet dinner at a rooftop restaurant with panoramic views over the rice fields or ocean.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before yoga — banana, coffee, and toast at a local café, ~IDR 30,000–60,000
meals.lunch: Eat what you cooked in the cooking class — a full Balinese feast!
meals.dinner: Rooftop restaurant or warung — keep it light after a big lunch, perhaps a fresh salad, grilled vegetables, and soup, ~IDR 80,000–150,000

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class at least 2–3 days in advance. Many classes include pickup and drop-off from your hotel. This is one of the most memorable and educational experiences in Bali — highly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Bali Botanic Garden (Kebun Raya Bali) in Bedugul — a stunning highland garden at 1,400m altitude with over 2,000 plant species. Enjoy the cool mountain air and peaceful atmosphere. Combine with a stop at the beautiful Pura Ulun Danu Bratan — a water temple set on the shores of Lake Bratan.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Bedugul area further — visit Bali Treetop Adventure Park for zip-lining and aerial obstacle courses through the forest canopy (~IDR 200,000–350,000). Then stop at a local strawberry farm in Candi Kuning — pick your own strawberries and buy fresh local produce.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort via a scenic mountain route. Stop for dinner in Ubud or along the way. Enjoy a relaxing evening at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before early departure
meals.lunch: Local restaurant near Lake Bratan — try corn fritters, vegetable soup, and fresh strawberry juice, ~IDR 60,000–120,000
meals.dinner: Ubud stop on the way back — duck or pork dish at a traditional Balinese restaurant, ~IDR 100,000–200,000

day_by_day.notes: Bedugul is about 1.5 hours from the coast — start early to maximize time. Bring a light jacket as the highlands are noticeably cooler (18–22°C). The drive through the mountain roads is scenic and worth enjoying slowly.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach day — spend the morning at your favorite beach discovered during the trip. Go for a long swim, practice yoga on the sand, or simply read and relax with a coconut. Reflect on the journey and savor the last full day in paradise.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping in Seminyak or Kuta — pick up handmade jewelry, batik sarongs, locally made skincare products, or Balinese wood carvings. Visit a local silver workshop in Celuk (near Ubud) if time permits, or browse boutiques in Seminyak.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell sunset cocktails at a rooftop or cliffside bar. Splurge slightly on a special farewell dinner at a nicer restaurant — this is your last night in Bali. Enjoy a full Balinese rijsttafel (rice table feast) or a romantic beachside dinner.

meals.breakfast: Favorite café from the trip — revisit a spot you loved
meals.lunch: Light beach lunch — fresh fruit, satay, and cold drinks, ~IDR 60,000–100,000
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner — Balinese rijsttafel or fine dining with ocean views, ~IDR 250,000–450,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Pack your bags tonight to make the morning departure stress-free. Leave out only what you need for the morning. Set multiple alarms. Consider tipping your regular driver, resort staff, and any guides who made your trip special.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise yoga or beach walk if your flight time permits. Enjoy a last breakfast at the resort. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort, settle any bills, and arrange airport transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Ngurah Rai International Airport. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for check-in, immigration, and security. Browse duty-free shops for last-minute gifts — Bali coffee, chocolate, and Krisbow products make great souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Bali with a heart full of memories, a relaxed body from yoga and spa treatments, sun-kissed skin, and a deep appreciation for the Island of the Gods.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — go all out one last time with a full tropical spread
meals.lunch: Airport restaurant or café — Bali-style nasi goreng one last time, ~IDR 80,000–150,000
meals.dinner: On the flight home

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your flight details and check-in online the night before. Keep your passport, boarding pass, and travel documents easily accessible. Bali's airport can be busy during peak season — arrive early. Safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Bali Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled – late night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled – late night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Ngurah Rai International Airport at 22:30. Private luxury transfer arranged by Aegean Bliss Resort awaits with a welcome sign, chilled towels, and refreshments. Check in to your Beachfront suite, enjoy a complimentary welcome drink and fruit basket prepared by the resort. Wind down with a warm shower and settle in.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable
meals.lunch: Not applicable
meals.dinner: Light late-night welcome platter and tropical fruit basket provided in-room by the resort upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Ensure your resort transfer is pre-booked. Keep luggage light for carry-on to speed through arrival. Immigration at Bali can be busy late evenings – have your e-visa and accommodation details ready. Rest well for the journey ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely start. Begin with a 7:30 AM sunrise beach walk along the private beachfront stretch of the resort. At 9:00 AM, join the resort's complimentary sunrise yoga session on the beachfront deck – a gentle Hatha flow to awaken the body and embrace the warm Bali morning air.
day_by_day.afternoon: After a late breakfast, spend the afternoon exploring the resort's private beach. Rent a paddleboard or kayak from the resort's water sports center. At 2:00 PM, book a 90-minute Balinese traditional massage at the resort's luxury spa to ease any travel fatigue.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy cocktail hour at the resort's beachfront infinity bar as the sun sets over the Indian Ocean. Dine at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant under open skies with ocean views.

meals.breakfast: Lavish buffet breakfast at the resort's main restaurant featuring tropical fruits, Balinese ceremonial rice porridge (bubur), eggs Benedict, freshly squeezed juices, and artisan coffee
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch at the resort's cabana bar – grilled seafood skewers, fresh coconut, and a mixed green salad
meals.dinner: Signature resort restaurant – pan-seared barramundi with lemongrass beurre blanc, prawn bisque starter, and a decadent chocolate lava cake for dessert paired with a curated Balinese wine selection

day_by_day.notes: This is your first full day – keep it relaxed and resort-based to recover from travel. July weather in Bali is dry and warm (~25°C), perfect for beach activities. Apply high-SPF sunscreen as UV levels are high even in warm overcast conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Rise at 6:30 AM for an invigorating Vinyasa Flow yoga class on the beach at sunrise led by the resort's resident yogi. Afterward, take a refreshing dip in the ocean. Return to your suite for a fresh-pressed juice and light snack before heading out.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private chauffeured tour to the iconic Tanah Lot Temple, one of Bali's most sacred sea temples perched dramatically on a rocky outcrop. Explore the temple grounds, photograph the dramatic coastal scenery, and learn about Balinese Hindu traditions from your private guide. Stop at a nearby artisan market for premium handcrafted souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort and unwind with a sunset cocktail at the infinity pool. Dine at a premium beachfront restaurant nearby, such as Sundara at Four Seasons Jimbaran for a world-class oceanfront dining experience.

meals.breakfast: À la carte breakfast at the resort – avocado toast with poached eggs, smoked salmon, and a matcha latte
meals.lunch: Casual beachside warung near Tanah Lot upgraded to a premium local dining experience – nasi campur (mixed rice platter) with grilled fish, tempeh, and sambal
meals.dinner: Sundara Beach Club, Jimbaran – tasting menu featuring fresh Jimbaran Bay seafood, sashimi-grade tuna, and signature cocktails with feet-in-the-sand dining ambiance

day_by_day.notes: Tanah Lot is approximately 30–45 minutes from the southern Bali beachfront area. Visit in the afternoon to avoid morning tour crowds. Dress modestly (sarong and sash required at the temple – provided at the entrance). Hire a private guide for the most enriching experience.

day_by_day.morning: Morning Yin Yoga and meditation session at 7:00 AM on the resort's beachfront yoga pavilion. Focus on deep stretching and breathwork to ground your energy for the day. Afterward, enjoy a slow breakfast and prepare for a full-day beach exploration.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private boat charter to explore the crystal-clear waters off the Bali coast. Snorkel at a pristine reef system teeming with tropical fish and vibrant coral. Stop at a secluded sandbar for a private champagne picnic lunch prepared by the resort's culinary team. Return by 4:00 PM and enjoy the resort's spa steam room and hydrotherapy pool.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Kecak fire dance performance at Uluwatu Temple at sunset (approximately 6:00 PM). The dramatic cliffside setting and ancient performance art make for an unforgettable cultural evening.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet with a focus on wellness – acai bowls, chia pudding, granola with Balinese honey, and herbal teas
meals.lunch: Private champagne picnic on the sandbar – gourmet sandwiches, fresh fruit, chilled prawns, sparkling wine, and artisan chocolates prepared by the resort chef
meals.dinner: Rock Bar at AYANA Resort, Uluwatu – dramatic cliffside dining with ocean views, premium cocktails, and a curated menu of modern Asian cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Book the private boat charter and Kecak performance tickets at least 48 hours in advance through the resort's concierge. The Kecak performance at Uluwatu is one of Bali's most iconic cultural experiences – arrive 30 minutes early for the best viewing positions. Bring a light wrap for the evening sea breeze.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Ubud – depart at 8:00 AM by private chauffeured car (approximately 1.5 hours). Begin with a visit to the Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary, a lush nature reserve home to hundreds of Balinese long-tailed macaques. Stroll the ancient temple grounds and jungle pathways.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ubud's famous Tegallalang Rice Terraces – walk through the stunning stepped paddies and photograph the UNESCO-recognized landscape. Visit a premium local art gallery on Ubud's main street, then stop at a luxury wellness center for a traditional Jamu herbal drink experience and a short sound healing session.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Ubud at one of the island's most celebrated restaurants before the private transfer back to the resort (depart Ubud by 8:30 PM).

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the resort before departure – fresh fruit, yogurt parfait, and espresso
meals.lunch: Locavore NXT, Ubud – Bali's celebrated farm-to-table concept restaurant with a seasonal tasting menu sourced from local organic farms and foraged ingredients
meals.dinner: Swept Away at Como Shambhala Estate, Ubud – romantic riverside fine dining in a jungle setting with contemporary Indonesian cuisine and an exceptional wine list

day_by_day.notes: Ubud is approximately 1.5 hours from the southern beach resort area – an early departure ensures maximum time to explore. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the rice terraces and monkey forest. Keep valuables secure around the monkeys as they are known to snatch items. The return journey at night is smooth on the main highway.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated wellness morning – begin with a 6:30 AM pranayama (breathwork) and meditation session on your private beachfront balcony or the resort's yoga pavilion. At 8:30 AM, book a 2-hour Balinese Royal Lulur body treatment at the resort spa – a traditional royal scrub using turmeric, rice powder, and jasmine followed by a floral milk bath.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend a blissful afternoon at the resort's private beach. Try stand-up paddleboarding in the calm July waters. At 3:00 PM, enjoy a private surf lesson with a certified instructor in the gentle beach break near the resort – perfect for beginners and intermediate surfers alike.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cocktails at the resort's infinity pool bar watching the golden hour light play over the Indian Ocean. Enjoy a private in-suite dining experience – a romantic beachside dinner set up on your private terrace by the resort's butler service.

meals.breakfast: In-suite breakfast delivered to your terrace – eggs your way, smoked salmon bagel, fresh tropical fruit platter, and cold-pressed green juice
meals.lunch: Resort pool bar – wagyu beef sliders, truffle fries, fresh coconut water, and a chilled Aperol Spritz
meals.dinner: Private in-suite beachfront terrace dinner curated by the resort chef – lobster thermidor, saffron risotto, artisan cheese board, and a bottle of Whispering Angel rosé

day_by_day.notes: The Balinese Lulur treatment should be booked through the resort spa at least one day in advance. This is a perfect mid-trip wellness reset day. The private in-suite dinner experience may require advance arrangement with the butler – request it the evening before. July surf conditions are generally mellow on the southern coast, ideal for lessons.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning excursion to witness the sunrise at Mount Batur, Bali's active volcano. Depart the resort at 2:00 AM by private vehicle (approximately 2 hours to the trailhead). Begin the guided trek at 4:00 AM with a certified mountain guide, reaching the 1,717m summit by sunrise at approximately 6:00 AM. Enjoy a breakfast of hard-boiled eggs cooked in volcanic steam at the summit – a unique Bali tradition.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend the volcano by 9:00 AM and visit the natural hot springs at Toya Devasya for a restorative soak in geothermal mineral pools overlooking Lake Batur. Enjoy a lakeside lunch before the private transfer back to the resort (arrive approximately 3:00 PM). Rest and recover at the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Gentle restorative yoga session at the resort at 6:00 PM to ease muscles after the trek. Light and nourishing dinner at the resort's wellness restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Volcanic summit breakfast – hard-boiled eggs steamed in volcanic vents, bananas, and hot ginger tea provided by the guide
meals.lunch: Toya Devasya lakeside restaurant – grilled tilapia from Lake Batur, steamed rice, local vegetables, and fresh coconut
meals.dinner: Resort wellness restaurant – superfood Buddha bowl with tempeh, avocado, edamame, and miso dressing; ginger and turmeric recovery tonic

day_by_day.notes: The Mount Batur sunrise trek is one of Bali's most iconic experiences. Book a certified guide through the resort concierge – do not attempt without one. Wear layers as the summit temperature can drop to 10°C before sunrise. Bring a headlamp, trekking poles, and sturdy shoes. The trek is moderately challenging (2–3 hours up). This is a very early start day – plan to sleep early on Day 6.

day_by_day.morning: Full rest and recovery morning after the Mount Batur trek. Sleep in until 9:00 AM. Enjoy a slow, indulgent morning on your private beachfront terrace. Light stretching and a gentle 30-minute walk along the shoreline to reconnect with the ocean.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the premium Waterbom Bali water park in Kuta (approximately 20 minutes from the resort) for a fun and luxurious afternoon – upgrade to a private cabana with dedicated service. Enjoy thrilling slides and lazy river experiences in a beautifully landscaped tropical setting. Return to the resort by 5:00 PM.
day_by_day.evening: Beachfront bonfire experience arranged by the resort – enjoy s'mores, tropical cocktails, and live acoustic Balinese music under the stars. Ideal for a relaxed, social evening.

meals.breakfast: Resort in-room dining – full American breakfast with pancakes, crispy bacon, scrambled eggs, fresh OJ, and strong Bali arabica coffee
meals.lunch: Waterbom Bali private cabana dining – gourmet burgers, fresh salads, and tropical smoothies served poolside
meals.dinner: Beachfront bonfire dinner at the resort – BBQ grilled seafood platter, corn on the cob, tropical fruit skewers, and signature cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Waterbom Bali is consistently rated one of Asia's best water parks. Book a private cabana in advance for the full luxury experience. This is intentionally a lighter activity day to allow full recovery from the Mount Batur trek. The beachfront bonfire experience can be arranged through the resort concierge – request it in the morning.

day_by_day.morning: 7:00 AM Ashtanga yoga session at the resort's beachfront pavilion with the resident yogi. Focus on building strength and flexibility through the dynamic primary series. Afterward, enjoy a healthy post-yoga smoothie bowl at the resort's juice bar.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided cultural tour of Seminyak and Canggu – explore the vibrant beach towns known for their world-class surf beaches, bohemian boutiques, and art galleries. Visit Batu Bolong Beach in Canggu to watch local surfers and soak in the laid-back creative atmosphere. Browse premium local designer boutiques for unique Balinese fashion and homeware.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at La Brisa beach club, Canggu – one of Bali's most celebrated beach clubs built from reclaimed fishing boats. Enjoy craft cocktails and live DJ sets as the sun dips below the horizon. Dine at a top Canggu restaurant before returning to the resort.

meals.breakfast: Resort juice bar post-yoga – dragon fruit and banana smoothie bowl topped with granola, coconut flakes, and local honey, plus a cold brew coffee
meals.lunch: Sensorium at The Layar, Seminyak – elevated Indonesian cuisine in a stunning villa setting with a curated cocktail menu
meals.dinner: Mejekawi by Ku De Ta, Seminyak – avant-garde Indonesian fine dining with a tasting menu that reimagines traditional Balinese flavors with modern culinary techniques

day_by_day.notes: Canggu and Seminyak are approximately 20–30 minutes from the southern beachfront resort area. Traffic can be heavier in the late afternoon – plan the return journey accordingly. La Brisa beach club is extremely popular at sunset; arrive by 5:00 PM to secure good seating. Dress code at Mejekawi is smart casual.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise sailing excursion departing from the resort's beach at 6:00 AM aboard a luxury catamaran. Sail along the stunning southern Bali coastline as the sun rises over the volcanic peaks. Enjoy champagne, fresh fruit, and pastries on deck. Snorkel at a pristine reef en route, teeming with sea turtles and tropical marine life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to shore by noon. Spend the afternoon at the resort's luxury spa with a comprehensive 3-hour spa journey: aromatherapy massage, facial, and reflexology foot treatment. This is the ultimate mid-afternoon indulgence.
day_by_day.evening: Private beachside candlelit dinner for two arranged on the resort's beach – a bespoke 6-course tasting menu prepared exclusively by the resort's executive chef with wine pairings. A truly romantic and memorable evening.

meals.breakfast: Champagne breakfast on the sailing catamaran – smoked salmon blinis, fresh tropical fruit, croissants, and sparkling wine on the open sea
meals.lunch: Light resort poolside lunch post-spa – chilled gazpacho, grilled prawn salad, and sparkling water with fresh mint
meals.dinner: Private 6-course beachside tasting menu by the resort's executive chef – courses include tuna tartare, lobster bisque, wagyu beef tenderloin, a Balinese cheese selection, and a passion fruit soufflé with wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: The private sailing excursion and beachside private dinner must be booked through the resort concierge at least 2–3 days in advance. This is the most romantic and indulgent day of the trip – ideal for celebrating a special occasion. The 3-hour spa journey should also be pre-booked. Bring reef-safe sunscreen for the snorkeling portion.

day_by_day.morning: 7:30 AM partner yoga and acro-yoga workshop at the resort's yoga studio – a fun and playful session for two focused on trust, balance, and connection. Afterward, take a long leisurely beach walk and collect shells along the shoreline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Day trip to the Nusa Dua area – visit the premium BNDCC (Bali Nusa Dua Convention Centre) beach promenade and the pristine Geger Beach, one of Bali's most exclusive and uncrowded beaches. Enjoy water sports including jet skiing and parasailing. Visit the Grand Hyatt Bali's legendary beachfront for afternoon drinks.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a farewell-adjacent evening of reflection. Enjoy a private rooftop or beachfront stargazing experience arranged by the resort, complete with a telescope, expert guide, and a curated dessert and cocktail spread.

meals.breakfast: Resort restaurant – eggs Florentine, fresh fruit platter, Balinese black rice pudding with coconut cream, and a fresh turmeric latte
meals.lunch: Kayuputi Restaurant at St. Regis Bali, Nusa Dua – one of Bali's finest beachfront fine-dining experiences with contemporary Asian cuisine and a stunning lagoon setting
meals.dinner: Stargazing dessert spread at the resort – artisan cheese and charcuterie board, chocolate fondue with tropical fruits, macarons, and premium cocktails under the Bali night sky

day_by_day.notes: Nusa Dua is approximately 15–20 minutes from the southern resort area. Kayuputi at St. Regis is one of Bali's most acclaimed restaurants – reservations are essential and should be made several days in advance. The stargazing experience should be arranged with the resort concierge the day before. July skies in Bali are typically clear and excellent for stargazing.

day_by_day.morning: Final full morning yoga practice – a 90-minute integrative yoga and meditation session at 7:00 AM combining all the styles practiced throughout the trip: pranayama, Vinyasa, Yin, and Savasana meditation. A mindful closing of the wellness journey. Afterward, swim in the ocean one last time and take photographs of the resort and beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisure shopping and exploration in Seminyak's premium boutique strip – browse high-end Balinese fashion at Biasa, premium homewares at Coco de Mer, and bespoke jewelry at John Hardy. Stop for a cold-pressed juice at a local wellness café. Return to the resort by 4:00 PM and begin light packing.
day_by_day.evening: Grand farewell dinner at one of Bali's most iconic fine-dining establishments. Reflect on the journey with exceptional food, wine, and atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Resort – full Balinese breakfast experience: nasi goreng (fried rice), satay lilit (minced fish satay), jukut urap (vegetable salad with coconut), and fresh coconut water
meals.lunch: Revolver Espresso, Seminyak – artisan sandwiches, specialty coffee, and fresh pastries in Bali's most celebrated specialty coffee institution
meals.dinner: Sarong Restaurant, Seminyak – Bali's legendary fine-dining institution with a globally inspired tasting menu, an award-winning wine cellar, and an intimate, jewel-box dining room atmosphere

day_by_day.notes: Sarong Restaurant requires advance reservations and is one of the most sought-after tables in Bali – book at least 3–4 days ahead through the concierge. This is your last full evening in Bali – savor every moment. If time permits, request the resort to arrange a professional photographer for a final sunset photoshoot on the beach as a lasting memory of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Bali – wake up for one last sunrise on the beach. Enjoy a quiet and reflective 20-minute seated meditation facing the ocean. Take a final dip in the resort pool or ocean. Complete packing and check out formalities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time, enjoy a final poolside or beachfront lunch at the resort. If time allows, visit a nearby local market for any last-minute authentic Balinese souvenirs – handwoven textiles, Balinese silver jewelry, organic coconut products, and artisan spices make wonderful gifts. Resort checkout and private luxury transfer to Ngurah Rai International Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Bali. Carry with you the memories of 13 extraordinary days of beaches, yoga, culture, and world-class luxury on the Island of the Gods.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast – a full spread of favorites from the past 13 days: tropical fruits, Balinese porridge, avocado toast, and a farewell Bali coffee
meals.lunch: Final poolside lunch at the resort – grilled barracuda fish tacos, fresh coconut, and a tropical fruit sorbet as a sweet farewell
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight premium dining (coordinate with airline for special meal requests in advance)

day_by_day.notes: Check-out time at most Bali resorts is 12:00 PM – request a late check-out (until 2:00 PM or 3:00 PM) through the concierge if your flight is in the evening. Arrange airport transfer at least 3 hours before your flight departure. Bali's airport can be busy – arrive with ample time. Ensure all duty-free purchases comply with your destination country's customs regulations. Terima kasih, Bali – until next time.
